files.document_title: Glennallen to Palmer Spur Line, Alignment and Lands, Appendix A to the Engineering Report, prepared for the Alaska Natural Gas Development Authority by Michael Baker Jr., Inc., April 4, 2005 (25 sheets, drawing numbers 105043-001 onward)
files.what_it_shows: A full set of 24 land use and ownership alignment sheets for the whole proposed line from Glennallen to Palmer. Each sheet shows the centerline over a topographic base with milepost numbers, a UTM Zone 6 (NAD 83, meters) grid with labeled coordinates, land ownership, stream crossings and an elevation profile. The first sheet covers milepost 0.00 to 5.95 and the line starts at the Trans-Alaska Pipeline right-of-way. This is the proposed route that the 2005 right-of-way lease application describes.

files.document_title: Same document, sheet 2 (drawing 105043-001), milepost 0.00 to 5.95, rendered at 150 dpi
files.what_it_shows: The start of the line near Glennallen, running east to west along a section line north of the Glenn Highway, with a UTM grid and ownership.

files.document_title: Same document, sheet 12 (drawing 105043-011), milepost 62.30 to 68.34, rendered at 150 dpi
files.what_it_shows: A mid-route sheet where the line runs beside the Glenn Highway and then follows Squaw Creek, with the UTM grid, section numbers, mileposts and an Alaska Natural Gas Development Authority block valve site.

files.document_title: ANGDA right-of-way lease application, Glennallen to Palmer Spur Line, 2005 (22 pages)
files.what_it_shows: Text only, no map. It states the route is about 148 miles of 24-inch pipe, begins at the Trans-Alaska Pipeline right-of-way about 2 miles north of Glennallen on Ahtna lands, follows the Glenn Highway right-of-way for almost 50 miles, then an RS-2477 trail up the Squaw and Caribou Creek drainages, over Chitna Pass and down Boulder Creek into Chickaloon, then mostly an existing Matanuska Electric Association route to Palmer. It points to the alignment sheets in Appendix A of the Engineering Report.

searched: The attached 2005 right-of-way lease application on the Alaska Resources Library and Information Services site, read in full
The directory listings on arlis.org for the Alaska gas collection, which turned up the Map folder with the Appendix A alignment sheets
Not searched further because a legible full-route map set was found: Alaska Department of Natural Resources case files, the Regulatory Commission of Alaska
notes: The alignment sheets are on the same website as the lease application but in a different folder, so the seed document itself has no map. The sheets carry a labeled UTM Zone 6 grid on every page, so a person can fit them to the ground with independently sourced control points such as the Glenn Highway, the Trans-Alaska Pipeline and named creek crossings. Only a few sheets were opened and viewed (sheets 2 and 12); the others were rendered but not each inspected. The base is a scanned fax-quality copy and some text is upside down on the topographic layer. The sheets give 2005 mileposts; the application says route adjustments were expected after survey.
